output: html_notebook

```{r}
#rm(list=ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DESeq2)
library(tximport)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ensembldb)
library(RMariaDB)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

library(biomaRt)
```
  The RNA-seq data contains 2 conditions: 4T1-Ctrl, 4T1-TGFb (10ng/mL for 24hr). With 3 repliates each.
  First, RNA-seq reads were quantified using Salmon/1.8.0. 
  Transcriptome version: GRCm39, Ensembl 111

1. We will import count files using tximport.
```{r}
# Load metadata and tx2gene file
dir <- "/Users/xiaohanning/Partners HealthCare Dropbox/Ning Xiaohan/BT549_4T1_TGFb_bulk_rnaseq"
meta_4T1 <- read.table(file.path(dir,"Analysis/4T1_TGFb_metadata.csv"), sep=",",header=T)
meta_4T1$Condition <- factor(meta_4T1$Condition)
meta_4T1$Genotype <- factor(meta_4T1$Genotype)
txdb_Mus <- makeTxDbFromEnsembl(organism="Mus musculus", release=111)
k_Mus <- keys(txdb_Mus, keytype="TXNAME")
tx2gene_Mus <- select(txdb_Mus, k_Mus, "GENEID", "TXNAME")
# Load Salmon output using tximport
files_4T1 <- file.path(dir,paste("Salmon/results/salmon_Mus/",meta_4T1$Sample,"_salmon", sep=""),"quant.sf")
names(files_4T1)<-meta_4T1$Sample
txi_data_4T1 <- tximport(files_4T1, type="salmon",tx2gene=tx2gene_Mus, ignoreTxVersion = T)
write.table(txi_data_4T1$counts, file = file.path(dir, "Analysis/gene_counts_4T1.txt"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE)
```

2. Make DEseq dataset
```{r}
names(txi_data_4T1)
head(txi_data_4T1$counts)
dds_4T1 <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi_data_4T1, colData = meta_4T1, design = ~Condition)
colnames(dds_4T1) <- meta_4T1$Sample
dds_4T1
```

```{r}
# Data QC, remove genes with low counts
keep_4T1 <- rowSums(counts(dds_4T1)) >= 10
dds_4T1 <- dds_4T1[keep_4T1,]
```

```{r}
# Run DESeq
dds_4T1 <- DESeq(dds_4T1) 
resultsNames(dds_4T1) #what does this do?
```

```{r}
dds_4T1 <- readRDS(file.path(dir, "Analysis/4T1_TGFb_deseq2.rds"))
res_4T1 <- results(dds_4T1, contrast=c("Condition","TGFb","Ctrl")) #TGFb vs Ctrl
saveRDS(dds_4T1, file.path(dir, "Analysis/4T1_TGFb_deseq2.rds"))
```

resLFC_4T1

plotMA(resLFC_4T1, ylim=c(-3,3))  # export 5, 5

```{r}
# RNA
genenames_mouse <- select(org.Mm.eg.db, keys= keys(org.Mm.eg.db, keytype="ENSEMBL"), columns=c("SYMBOL", "ENSEMBL"), keytype="ENSEMBL")
resfile_4T1 <- res_4T1
filename_4T1 <- "4T1_TGFb_vs_Ctrl.deseq2_output.tsv"
plotname_4T1 <- "4T1-TGFb vs 4T1-Ctrl"

  resp_table_4T1 <- merge(as.data.frame(resfile_4T1), genenames_mouse, by.x=0, by.y="ENSEMBL")
  resp_table_4T1 <- resp_table_4T1[!duplicated(resp_table_4T1$SYMBOL),]
  resp_table_4T1 <- resp_table_4T1 %>% remove_rownames() %>% column_to_rownames(var = "SYMBOL")
  resp_table_4T1 <- resp_table_4T1[order(resp_table_4T1$padj), ]
  Volcano_4T1 <- EnhancedVolcano(resp_table_4T1, lab=rownames(resp_table_4T1), x="log2FoldChange", y="padj", title= plotname_4T1, xlim = c(-8,8), ylim=c(0,120), pointSize = 1, pCutoff=10e-5, FCcutoff=1, labSize=4) # One or more p-values is 0. Converting to 10^-1 * current lowest non-zero p-value
  print(Volcano_4T1)
  
  write.table(resp_table_4T1, file=file.path(dir,"DEseq2",filename_4T1), sep='\t', row.names=T)
  resSig_4T1 <- subset(resp_table_4T1, padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > 0.5)
  resSig_4T1 <- resSig_4T1[order(-resSig_4T1$log2FoldChange),] # Descending
  print(str(sum(resSig_4T1$log2FoldChange > 0)), str(sum(resSig_4T1$log2FoldChange < 0)))
  write.table(resSig_4T1, file=paste(dir, "/DEseq2/",plotname_4T1,".deseq2_significant.tsv",sep=""), sep='\t', row.names=T)
```
   
3. Prepare dataset for GSEA   
```{r}
norm_counts_4T1 <- as.data.frame(counts(dds_4T1, normalized=T))
norm_counts_4T1 <- cbind(DESCRIPTION = "na", norm_counts_4T1)
write.table(norm_counts_4T1, file=file.path(dir, "GSEA/norm_counts_4T1.txt"), sep="\t")
# norm_counts_4T1 <- read.table("/Users/xiaohanning/Partners HealthCare Dropbox/Ning Xiaohan/BT549_4T1_TGFb_bulk_rnaseq/GSEA/norm_counts_4T1.txt")
genenames_mouse <- select(org.Mm.eg.db, keys= keys(org.Mm.eg.db, keytype="ENSEMBL"), columns=c("SYMBOL", "ENSEMBL"), keytype="ENSEMBL")
norm_genes_4T1 <- merge(as.data.frame(norm_counts_4T1), genenames_mouse, by.x=0, by.y="ENSEMBL")
norm_genes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1[!duplicated(norm_genes_4T1$SYMBOL),]
norm_genes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1 %>% remove_rownames() %>% column_to_rownames(var = "SYMBOL")
norm_genes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1[, -1] # remove Ensembl column
write.table(norm_genes_4T1, file=file.path(dir, "GSEA/norm_genes_4T1.txt"), sep="\t")
```
```{r}
matchMMUsymbol<-function(mouse_symbol){
	map=read.table(file.path(dir,'GSEA/Mouse_Human_GeneIDs_sub.txt'),sep=' ',header=T)
	map_sor<-map[match(mouse_symbol,map$mmu_symbol),]
	human<-map_sor$hsa_symbol
	return(human)
}
human_genes <- matchMMUsymbol(rownames(norm_genes_4T1))
norm_genes_4T1$human_genes <- matchMMUsymbol(rownames(norm_genes_4T1))
norm_genes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1[!duplicated(norm_genes_4T1$human_genes),]
norm_genes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1[!is.na(norm_genes_4T1$human_genes)&!(norm_genes_4T1$human_genes==""),]
norm_hgenes_4T1 <- norm_genes_4T1 %>% remove_rownames() %>% column_to_rownames(var = "human_genes")
write.table(norm_hgenes_4T1, file=file.path(dir, "GSEA/norm_human_genes_4T1.txt"), sep="\t")
```

mart <- useEnsembl(biomart="ensembl",mirror="useast")

mouse <- useEnsembl('ensembl', dataset = 'mmusculus_gene_ensembl',mirror="www")

  attributes = c('mgi_symbol','ensembl_gene_id','gene_biotype'),

}

4. Retrieve glycosylation-related genes
```{r}
# Install if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("clusterProfiler")
BiocManager::install("org.Hs.eg.db")  # For human gene annotation
BiocManager::install("KEGGREST")      # For accessing KEGG pathway information
install.packages("biomaRt")

# Load the required packages
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)  # Replace with appropriate organism database if needed
library(KEGGREST)
library(biomaRt)


# Connect to Ensembl BioMart
ensembl <- useMart("ensembl", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl")

# Retrieve all GO terms with descriptions
go_terms <- getBM(attributes = c("go_id", "name_1006"), mart = ensembl)

# Filter GO terms related to glycosylation
glycosylation_terms <- go_terms[grep("glycosylation", go_terms$name_1006, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
print(glycosylation_terms)

# Define glycosylation-related GO terms
go_glycosylation_terms <- c("GO:0070085",  # glycosylation
                            "GO:0006486",  # protein glycosylation
                            "GO:0006487",  # protein N-linked glycosylation
                            "GO:0016757",  # Glycosyltransferase activity
                            "GO:0008373")  # Sialyltransferase activity
                            
                            
# Retrieve genes associated with these GO terms
go_gene_list <- bitr(go_glycosylation_terms, fromType="GO", toType="SYMBOL", OrgDb="org.Hs.eg.db")
go_genes <- unique(go_gene_list$SYMBOL)

# Define the KEGG pathway ID for N-Glycan biosynthesis
kegg_pathway <- "hsa00510"

# Retrieve pathway information using KEGGREST
pathway_info <- keggGet(kegg_pathway)

# Extract gene information from the pathway
genes_info <- pathway_info[[1]]$GENE

# Extract the gene symbols from the gene information
# The GENE information is usually in pairs, with the gene ID and gene symbol
kegg_genes <- genes_info[seq(2, length(genes_info), by = 2)]
# Remove full name; only keep short gene symbols in front of ";".
kegg_genes <- sub(";.*", "", genes_info[seq(2, length(genes_info), by = 2)])

# View the first few gene symbols
head(kegg_genes)


# Combine the gene lists
Human_Glycan_genes <- unique(c(go_genes, kegg_genes))

# Display the combined list of genes
head(Human_Glycan_genes)

write.table(Human_Glycan_genes, file = paste0(dir, "/Glycosylation/Human_Glycan_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)


# Convert human gene list to mouse gene list

#1. Using Ensembl BioMart:
#Step 1: Go to Ensembl BioMart. http://useast.ensembl.org/biomart/martview/ddb6a8a9b63022bac899752b346fc273

#Step 2: Select the database Ensembl Genes and choose Homo sapiens as your dataset.
#Step 3: Under Filters, expand the GENE section and input your human gene symbols in the "Gene names" filter.
#Step 4: Under Attributes, go to Homologs and select Mouse orthologs. Choose Mouse gene name or Mouse Ensembl gene ID.
#Step 5: Click Results to get the corresponding mouse gene symbols.
#Step 6: Edit - remove blank rows, human column, save

mouse_Glycan_genes <- read.csv(file.path(dir,"Glycosylation/mouse_Glycan_genes.csv"), sep=",",header=T)

```

5. Virtualize glycosylation-related genes
```{r}
# Step 1: Convert csv into character
mouse_Glycan_genes <- as.character(mouse_Glycan_genes)

# Step 2: Clean up the string by removing unwanted characters
mouse_Glycan_genes <- gsub("c\\(|\\)", "", mouse_Glycan_genes)

# Step 3: Split the string into a vector
mouse_Glycan_genes <- unlist(strsplit(mouse_Glycan_genes, split = ",\\s*"))

# Step 4: Remove any remaining quotes
mouse_Glycan_genes <- gsub("\"", "", mouse_Glycan_genes)

# Now `gene_vector` is a clean character vector of gene names
print(mouse_Glycan_genes)

# Label glyco-related genes in Volcano plot
Volcano_4T1_glyco <- EnhancedVolcano(resp_table_4T1, lab=rownames(resp_table_4T1), x="log2FoldChange", y="padj", selectLab = mouse_Glycan_genes, title= plotname_4T1, xlim = c(-8,8), ylim=c(0,120), pointSize = 1, pCutoff=10e-5, FCcutoff=0.25, labSize=4)  # One or more p-values is 0. Converting to 10^-1 * current lowest non-zero p-value
  print(Volcano_4T1_glyco) # export 7.5, 10
  

# Retrieve glyco-related DGE (padj < 0.05)
Glycan_genes_4T1 <- subset(resp_table_4T1, rownames(resp_table_4T1) %in% mouse_Glycan_genes & padj < 0.05)
Glycan_genes_4T1 <- Glycan_genes_4T1[order(Glycan_genes_4T1$log2FoldChange,decreasing = T),]
write.table(Glycan_genes_4T1, file=paste(dir, "/Glycosylation/4T1_sig_Glycan_genes.tsv",sep=""), sep='\t', row.names=T)

# Extract the log2 fold changes
lfc_4T1_Glycan_genes <- as.matrix(Glycan_genes_4T1$log2FoldChange)

# Ensure row names (gene names) are preserved
rownames(lfc_4T1_Glycan_genes) <- rownames(Glycan_genes_4T1)

# Plot the heatmap
pheatmap(lfc_4T1_Glycan_genes,
         cluster_rows = FALSE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,  # Set to TRUE if you have multiple conditions (columns)
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,  # Set to TRUE if you have multiple conditions (columns)
         color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50),
         main = "Glycosylation-related gene: 4T1_TGFβ vs 4T1_Ctrl") # Zoom to ideal size, save image as png

```

Venn Diagram of overlapping genes between BT549 and 4T1
```{r}
install.packages("VennDiagram")
library(VennDiagram)

BT549_sig_Glycan_genes <- read.table(file.path(dir,"Glycosylation/BT549_sig_Glycan_genes.tsv"), sep="\t",header=T,row.names=1)
BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes <- BT549_sig_Glycan_genes[BT549_sig_Glycan_genes$log2FoldChange>0,]
write.table(BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes, file=file.path(dir,"Glycosylation/BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes.tsv"), sep='\t', row.names=T)

BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes <- rownames(BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes)

sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1 <- read.table(file.path(dir,"/Glycosylation/4T1_sig_up_Glycan_genes_convert_Human_symbol.tsv"), sep="\t",header=T)
sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1 <- sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1$Human.gene.name

# Generate the Venn diagram
venn.plot <- venn.diagram(
  x = list(
    List1 = BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes,
    List2 = sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1
  ),
  category.names = c("BT549", "4T1"),
  filename = NULL,  # To print directly to R plot viewer
  fill = c("grey", "orange"),
  alpha = 0.9,
  cat.cex = 2,
  cat.pos = c(-10, 10),
  cat.dist = c(0.06, 0.05),
  cat.col = c("black", "black"),
  cat.fontface = "bold",
  lwd = 3,
  cex = 0,  # Hide the counts
  main = "Glycan-related genes upregulated by TGFβ",
  main.fontface = "bold",
  main.cex = 2
)

# Draw the Venn diagram
grid.draw(venn.plot)

# Add labels for the overlapping genes

# Find the overlaps and unique genes
overlap_genes <- intersect(BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes, sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1)
unique_BT549 <- setdiff(BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes, sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1)
unique_4T1 <- setdiff(sig_up_Glycan_genes_4T1, BT549_sig_up_Glycan_genes)

# grid.text(
  #label = paste(overlap_genes, collapse = "\n"),
  #x = 0.52,   # X position of text (adjust as needed)
  #y = 0.55,   # Y position of text (adjust as needed)
 # gp = gpar(col = "black", fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")  # Customize appearance
#)

library(grid)

# Define the number of columns
num_columns <- 2

# Determine the number of genes per column
num_genes <- length(overlap_genes)
num_rows <- ceiling(num_genes / num_columns)

# Create a matrix with NA or empty strings to handle uneven column lengths
genes_matrix <- matrix(c(overlap_genes, rep(" ", num_columns * num_rows - num_genes)), 
                       nrow = num_rows, ncol = num_columns, byrow = TRUE)

# Draw text in columns
# grid.newpage()  # Start a new page for drawing

# Loop through the matrix and draw each gene in the correct position
for (i in 1:num_rows) {
  for (j in 1:num_columns) {
    grid.text(
      label = genes_matrix[i, j],
      x = 0.45 + (j - 1) * 0.14,  # Adjust x spacing for each column
      y = 0.58 - (i - 1) * 0.05,  # Adjust y spacing for each row
      just = c("center", "center"),
      gp = gpar(col = "black", fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold")
    )
  }
}

grid.draw(grobTree(
  grid.text("16", 
            x = 0.2,  # X position of text (adjust as needed)
            y = 0.47, # Y position of text (adjust as needed)
            gp = gpar(col="black", fontsize=20, fontface="bold")),
  grid.text("13", 
            x = 0.82, 
            y = 0.47, 
            gp = gpar(col="black", fontsize=20, fontface="bold"))
))

```
